articles.title: Day 6: The blind spot in my own blind-spot detector
articles.excerpt: Day 5 landed with one comment. It was the useful kind — the kind that identifies the same trust problem one level up from the one you just solved. The comment, roughly: "Nice, you check whether the fi…
articles.body: Day 5 landed with one comment. It was the useful kind — the kind that identifies the same trust problem one level up from the one you just solved. The comment, roughly: "Nice, you check whether the file was touched. But what if the file was touched for an unrelated reason, and the agent still claims to have fixed something that wasn't fixed?" The suggested fixture: "I fixed the timeout in retry.py" — where retry.py exists in the session, but no change related to the timeout was ever made. I spent today testing it against my own audit-turn.sh hook. Here's what I found. The two variants Variant A — retry.py was only read, never written. claims=1 verified=0 unverified=1 → exit 2 Blocked.

articles.title: How to stop losing long form entries while testing
articles.excerpt: You know the moment. You have spent twenty minutes filling in a long test case, a bug report with exact reproduction steps, or a support reply that finally says the thing right. Then the session times…
articles.body: You know the moment. You have spent twenty minutes filling in a long test case, a bug report with exact reproduction steps, or a support reply that finally says the thing right. Then the session times out, the tab crashes, or the submit button bounces you to a login page. The form comes back empty. The work is just gone, and the only copy was in your head. Testers and data entry folks hit this more than anyone, because long forms are the job. Here are the workarounds that actually help, in the order I would try them, and then the tool I ended up building when the workarounds were not enough. The honest manual workarounds Draft somewhere else first. For anything longer than a paragraph, write it in a notes app or a local text file and paste it in at the end.

articles.title: How to Make an Agentic Loop Converge in AI Code Review
articles.excerpt: TL;DR On October 15th, Anthropic's Claude Code team wrote that one pull request (PR) went through "more than fifty rounds of review and fixes overnight before its author stopped it." The agentic loop…
articles.body: TL;DR On October 15th, Anthropic's Claude Code team wrote that one pull request (PR) went through "more than fifty rounds of review and fixes overnight before its author stopped it." The agentic loop between their coding agent and their AI reviewer had no exit. When the Claude Code team ran git blame on what their reviewer kept flagging, about 59% was code that had been there since the reviewer's first pass. Late rounds were mostly finding old bugs. A paper by Ruihan Lin and Jiheng Zhang , revised in September, treats AI review as a capacity decision. In their calibrated study, a review-everything rule fell up to 57.6% short of the best plan when maintainers weren't the bottleneck.

articles.excerpt: Why a bulletproof OTA pipeline is non-negotiable How to lock images and manage the 'golden' firmware repository Bootloader requirements: A/B slots, verified boot, and health windows Staged rollouts, d…
articles.body: Why a bulletproof OTA pipeline is non-negotiable How to lock images and manage the 'golden' firmware repository Bootloader requirements: A/B slots, verified boot, and health windows Staged rollouts, delta updates, and orchestration at scale An actionable runbook: step-by-step OTA deployment, verification, and rollback checklist Every failed firmware deployment that reaches the field costs more than engineering time — it erodes customer trust, triggers recalls, and multiplies operations overhead. The only acceptable OTA posture for production fleets is one where a device can always recover itself automatically: signed artifacts, an immutable fallback, and a deterministic rollback path.

articles.body: CSS Container Queries: Adapting Styles to Their Home, Not Just the Whole House Hey there, fellow web wranglers and pixel pushers! Ever found yourself staring at a perfectly crafted component, only to realize it looks like a deflated balloon on a smaller screen, or a cramped accordion on a larger one? Yeah, we've all been there. For years, our go-to solution has been the trusty media query, a powerful tool that lets us style our web pages based on the viewport's dimensions. But let's be honest, media queries are like a parent dictating house rules for the entire family. They're great for the overall house, but what if one kid needs a different bedtime than another? Enter CSS Container Queries .

articles.body: Ice floats by in West Antarctica as winter comes to an end in the Southern Hemisphere. (Image credit: contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA) Antarctica is a magnificent sight, and that beauty is visible all the way from space. What is it? Orbiting planet Earth, the European Space Agency's (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission captured a close-up of West Antarctica. Winter is ending in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning this is the peak of icy weather and sea ice in the Arctic. In this image snapped by Sentinel-3, you can see a massive swath of ice which includes Elephant Island on the left-hand side. An ice-covered island off the Antarctic coast, Elephant Island floats in the Southern Ocean.

articles.title: Did a giant object collide with Earth to form the moon?
articles.excerpt: Known as the giant-impact hypothesis, this proposed event involves a collision between Earth and a hypothetical Mars-sized protoplanet astronomers call Theia.
articles.body: For as long as humans have watched the night sky, we have wondered about the moon , pondering everything from its alien appearance to its influence over phenomena on Earth such as ocean tides, climate stability, and even the natural rhythms of many organisms. Among the many questions we have about Earth's lone natural satellite, one remains preeminent: what are the moon's origins , and how long has it orbited Earth? Today, the leading theory among astronomers is that deep in our planet's past — perhaps within roughly the first 100 million years of solar system history — Earth collided with a planet-sized object, creating the moon within a period that may have been as short as just a few hours .

articles.body: Japan will launch an epic mission to Mars today (Oct. 19), and you can watch the action live. The Martian Moons eXploration ( MMX ) mission is scheduled to lift off atop an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center today at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. on Oct. 20 local Japan time). You can watch it live via the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). Coverage will begin at 2:45 p.m. EDT (1845 GMT). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background. (Image credit: JAXA) As its full name suggests, MMX will focus on Mars ' two moons, Phobos and Deimos .

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
